text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar wins support of UK Prime Minister John Major on Cuba conflict.
- A 53 year old man shot dead six people in Burgos, northern Spain and then killed himself.
- Administration minister Mariano Rajoy offers to increase salaries of public sector workers from 1998 if they call off their planned strike.
EL MUNDO
- Police find arms, money and documents in house of Juan Luis Aguirre Lete, a suspected ETA leader who was arrested on Tuesday.
DIARIO 16
- A man kills six people and then commits suicide in Burgos in a crime of passion.
- Aznar calls for calm after Cuba withdraws its acceptance of Spain's ambassador and hundreds of people gather around Spanish Embassy in Cuba.
CINCO DIAS
- Cost of money at new low of six percent as determined at Wednesday's auction of one-year bills.
- Companies take advantage of low interest rates and a high level of liquidity to demand favourable financing from banks.
- Social Security will modify base of contributions in January.
EXPANSION
- Argentaria develops a plan to overcome difficulties in its subsidiary Banco Exterior de Espana (BEX).
- IBM, Planeta and Telefonica have joined together to launch an offensive to develop use of Internet in Spain.
- Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato wants to accelerate liberalisation of real estate market.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Government will reduce number of public sector workers from 1998.
- Endesa's bid for electricity groups Sevillana and Fecsa has received an overwhelming acceptance by the two companies' shareholders.
- Industrial production falls 0.8 percent in September.
- Telefonica reduces prices in MoviStar by 11 percent. mad mcm
